official_measurement_examples.name: AQMA declaration trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: Under Local Air Quality Management, a local authority declares an AQMA where relevant air-quality objectives are not likely to be achieved; designation identifies a management problem rather than creating an automatic development ban.

official_measurement_examples.name: Action plan requirement
official_measurement_examples.fact: Where an AQMA is designated, the local authority must prepare an Air Quality Action Plan describing measures intended to improve air quality and work toward the objectives.

official_measurement_examples.name: Revoked AQMA distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: UK-AIR maintains a separate revoked-AQMA list, so historical AQMA geometry must not be treated as a current designation without checking status and dates.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning assessment is proposal-specific
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Practice Guidance says air quality relevance depends on the proposal and location and may require baseline, construction, operational, health and biodiversity assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning and permitting separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning guidance distinguishes air-quality assessment under planning from environmental permitting and states supporting assessments should not unnecessarily duplicate non-planning regulatory assessments.

official_measurement_examples.name: PM2.5 long-term targets
official_measurement_examples.fact: England's Air Quality Strategy records legally binding 2040 PM2.5 targets of an annual mean concentration of 10 micrograms per cubic metre or below and a 35 percent population-exposure reduction from the 2018 baseline.

official_measurement_examples.name: National assessment limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The supplementary modelling assessment for 2024, published 12 March 2026, assesses regulatory compliance using measured and modelled concentrations across national assessment zones; it is not a parcel-level planning clearance dataset.

official_measurement_examples.name: Protected-site air pollution distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Air-quality controls for human-health objectives, AQMA management, protected-site critical loads or levels, planning assessment and environmental permitting are related but distinct decision gates.

core_rules: AQMA designation is not an automatic development prohibition
AQMA status must retain declaration amendment and revocation dates
a revoked AQMA must not be represented as a current designation
Air Quality Action Plan measures are not planning permission
planning air-quality assessment must retain proposal and receptor context
national compliance modelling is not parcel-level concentration proof
monitoring-station data must not be silently extrapolated to every parcel
air-quality objectives and standards must retain pollutant and averaging period
PM2.5 national targets are not parcel-specific planning thresholds
environmental permitting is distinct from planning permission
protected-site critical loads and human-health AQMA objectives must not be merged
mitigation proposals are not proof residual effects are acceptable
air-quality evidence does not determine ownership access or transport capacity
historic model outputs must retain model year assumptions and uncertainty
no parcel air-quality clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
